coach_says: Fine move. You are a pawn up and f5 chases the bishop off its strong central square on e4. The bishop will usually grab b7 on its way, so you give that pawn back, but your knight, queen and safer king keep you clearly better. Quieter moves like Rad8 or Rab8 (covering b7 first) were just as good. If you want to avoid giving the pawn back, check which loose pawns a piece can take as it retreats.

Good enough: you are winning and Bd3 keeps the bishop aimed at h7. The knight on h7 is stuck there, attacked twice by your rooks and bishop, so it will fall soon anyway. Bxh7+ at once was the cleanest way to cash in. When an enemy piece is pinned and can't escape, taking it straight away is simpler than letting your opponent find counterplay with ...g4.
also: cash in on a trapped piece

coach_says: This was the engine's top move. Your bishop on d3 is attacked by the e4 pawn and has nowhere safe to go (c4, b5, a6 and e4 all lose it to a pawn), so you will lose material whichever move you play. Ng4 hits the rook on f6 first to gain a tempo before you give the bishop for a pawn with Bxe4. The real lesson came a move earlier: after 12.Nxe4 fxe4 the pawn attacked your bishop, and the bishop was boxed in by your own pawns.

In rook endgames, put your rook on the most active square before you move your pawns. Rd4 first took the whole fourth rank, attacked the b4 pawn, and after that f4 would have chased the black rook off e5. Played straight away, f4 left the e4 square for Black's rook: ...Re4 hits f4, then ...Rc4 goes after c2, and your extra pawn becomes hard to use. Next time, ask which squares a pawn move gives the enemy rook before you push it.
also: pawn move gives up a square

coach_says: Bxd4 loses a piece. Your knight on e2 was the only thing defending d4, and it was itself attacked by the rook on c2. Black plays ...Rxe2, and after Qxe2 Rxd4 they have two pieces for the rook, which is a big gain. First deal with the rook on your second rank, for example with Rc1 to trade it off, and only then take the d4 pawn. Before you capture, check that every piece guarding your capturing piece is safe.
also: deal with the rook on your 2nd rank
